source.author: Irina Alexandrovna Markovskaya
source.title: Linear groups over finite fields and over the ring of integers as automorphism groups of regular polytopes of rank 3

domain: n>=2, the intended domain fixed by both source tables and all case analyses; finite q is a prime power, odd q throughout the new Chapter 4 classifications.

definitions.admissible: Three involutions with a commuting pair, allowing repetitions and the trivial group as in source p11; equivalent operationally to order-at-most-two marks.
definitions.polytope: Rank-three abstract regular polytope, hence three distinct nonidentity string C-generators and the intersection property.

principal_claims.principal_conclusion: GL_n(Z) admissible iff n>=5; PGL_n(Z) admissible iff n=2 or n>=5.
route: I: final theorem and Sections 1–4, including both n=2 cases and all n>=5 words.
principal_claims.qualification: PSL_3(2) and PSL_4(2) nonadmissibility are explicitly retained external inputs. No rank-three polytope conclusion over Z is asserted by this theorem.

principal_claims.principal_conclusion: GL_n(q) admissible iff [q=2 and (n=2 or n>=5)] or [q=3 and n>=5].
route: L: Theorem labelled gl, Section 2.
I supplies L's previously retained integral existence premise for reduction modulo 3.
U supplies the complete symmetric-square obstruction for GL_4(3).
principal_claims.qualification: All q>=4 excluded by determinants; all n=3,4 excluded; GL_2(3) excluded directly. Source Table 1 is exactly these six cases.

principal_claims.principal_conclusion: GL_n(q) is a rank-three regular-polytope group iff q in {2,3} and n>=5.
route: L gives the complete admissibility exclusion list.
For q=3, GL_n(3)=H_n(3); H Theorem 1 gives generation and the actual intersection property.
For q=2, GL_n(2)=PSL_n(2) is simple for n>=5; retained simple admissibility and Conder–Oliveros give a marking.
GL_2(2)=S3 has no distinct commuting involutions and hence no rank-three C-marking.
Q Section 3 writes this complete assembly; its distinct review is pending.
principal_claims.qualification: This is not a consequence of reducing integral generators alone. The replacement does not claim the precise source GL_6(3) marking or its pair orders 24 and 12.

principal_claims.hypotheses: Finite field q; intended n>=2; d=gcd(n,q−1).
principal_claims.principal_conclusion: PGL_n(q) admissible iff n=2, or n>=4 and d=2, or n>=5 and d=1.
route: L: Theorem labelled pgl, Section 5, acquiring Sections 2–4 and U.
I replaces the old integral input in the q=3,n=6 reuse branch.
principal_claims.qualification: For n=2 all q are positive, including q=2 by repeated marks. For n>=3, d>2 is excluded by the cyclic determinant quotient; n=3 is always negative; n=4,d=1 is negative. Source Table 2 is exactly these six cases.

principal_claims.hypotheses: Finite field q; intended n>=2; d=gcd(n,q−1).
principal_claims.principal_conclusion: PGL_n(q) is a rank-three regular-polytope group iff n=2 and q!=2, or n>=4 and d=2, or n>=5 and d=1.
route: L: Section 5, paragraph following its two classification tables.
Q Section 3 repeats the exact parameter route and explicitly supplies the S3 exclusion.
principal_claims.qualification: PGL_2(3)=S4 is not almost simple and is treated separately. For the other positive cases the simple-socle centralizer argument rules out cyclic normal subgroups. No blanket almost-simple assertion is retained.

principal_claims.hypotheses: Odd prime power q; intended n>=2; H_n(q)={g:det(g)=±1}.
route: H: Theorem 1, all constructions in Sections 1–4.
Z: Theorem labelled small gives the complete n=2,3,4 exclusions using U.
principal_claims.qualification: The characteristic-two sentence before the source theorem is background attributed to previous work, not an additional principal classification in this thesis.

principal_claims.principal_conclusion: H_n(q) is a rank-three regular-polytope group iff n>=5; for every n>=5 a type [4p,n] or [4p,2n] occurs.
route: H: Theorem 1 and Section 5, complete monomial-intersection calculation and exact product orders.
Z: n=2,3,4 nonadmissibility also excludes polytopes.
principal_claims.qualification: The disjunction of types means at least one displayed construction of one of those types; it is not a classification of all possible types, nor a claim both types occur for every parameter.

principal_claims.hypotheses: Odd q=p^m; even n>=6; Z1=Z(H_n(q)); d=gcd(n,q−1), e=(q−1)/d.
principal_claims.principal_conclusion: The full-centre quotient has a rank-three regular polytope of type [4p,n]. The printed universal isomorphism to PSL_n(q) semidirect C2 requires correction.
route: Z: Theorem labelled centres: H/Z1=PSL_n(q) for e even; H/Z1 embeds as PSL_n(q) semidirect C2 for e odd.
H: Theorem 2 with S=Z1 gives the type [4p,n] in both cases.
Q: final section records precisely this corrected principal disposition.
principal_claims.qualification: Source p69 falsely states Z1=Z2 for every even n. At n=6,q=5, 2I has determinant −1, |Z1|=4 and |Z2|=2. This is a correction to a numbered corollary, not just a harmless intermediate typo.

principal_claims.principal_conclusion: H_n(q)/Z1 is PSL_n(q), with a rank-three regular polytope of type [4p,n].
route: Z: Theorem centres; odd n makes e even.
H: Theorem 2 with S=Z1.
principal_claims.qualification: The source corollary uses the full centre Z1. It must not be swapped with Corollary 4.2.3, which uses Z2.

principal_claims.principal_conclusion: H_n(q)/Z2 is PSL_n(q) × C2, with a rank-three regular polytope of type [4p,n] or [4p,2n].
route: Z: Theorem centres; the central factor is represented by −I.
H: Theorem 2 with S=Z2.
principal_claims.qualification: No almost-simple criterion is applied to this direct product. Its cyclic normal factor makes that criterion inapplicable; the actual quotient intersection proof supplies the asserted types.

principal_claims.principal_conclusion: Q_n(q) admissible iff n=2 and q!=9, or n>=4.
route: Q: Lemma 1 and Theorem 2 close n=2,3; distinct review pending.
Z: Theorem qfour supplies every odd field in n=4.
H: Theorem 2 with S=Z2 supplies all n>=5.
principal_claims.qualification: For n=2, q=7 is positive through PGL_2(7), despite PSL_2(7) being excluded. q=9 is negative via its PSL_2(9) quotient. All n=3 are negative. The defective source beta on p72 is replaced by the reviewed N011 construction.

principal_claims.principal_conclusion: Q_n(q) is a rank-three regular-polytope group iff n=2 and q!=9, or n>=4.
route: Q: Lemma 1 and Theorem 2, with the actual central-lift proof from Z; distinct review pending.
Z: qfour covers n=4 without asserting every displayed triple has IP in the direct-product case.
H: actual scalar-quotient marking covers n>=5.
principal_claims.qualification: The source blanket invocation of Lemma 1.3.2 cannot cover Q when it has a central C2. Use the perfect-group central lift or H's direct quotient intersection proof.
